propositions: When an ordered pair holds two net-active relations (e.g., blocks and relates_to), peer deletion of one relation causes the inbound removal record to reach guard G5 and decline permanently because write is relation-scoped but removal is pair-scoped.

The outbound differ dedupes direction-agnostically on (vendor_type, target_key) but not on relation, allowing same-vendor-type remote links in opposite directions to suppress outbound ADD emissions, which prevents inbound remove records from being suppressed by guard G4.

Inbound link removal never converges for a double-related pair when the outbound differ emits no mutation for that pair, because the G5 decline is permanent and the removal record re-emits and re-declines on every subsequent pass.

The fix makes removal symmetric with write by introducing relation-scoped removal keyed on (target_id, relation) at the graph layer and threading the relation through the reconciler's inbound unlink path.
CLI unlink gains an optional relation argument; with no relation the existing pair-scoped most-recent behavior is unchanged for backward compatibility.
Safety invariant is preserved: a removal naming a relation with no matching net-active local link is a logged no-op and never removes a different relation or a link the peer still carries.
